 Gonzaga team looking to turn page from LSU loss hosts Big Sky favorite Montana State
 Nov. 16, 2026 
 Updated Mon., Nov. 16, 2026 at 7:24 p.m. 
 Gonzaga Bulldogs center Massamba Diop, left, and forward Braden Huff low-five during college basketball action against the LSU Tigers on Saturday at the Spokane Arena. (Tyler Tjomsland / The Spokesman-Review)
 Add Spokesman-Review on Google
 By 
 Theo Lawson theol@spokesman.com (509) 459-5584 
 Related

 Someone could point to any number of records, streaks or statistical anomalies to highlight Gonzaga’s sustained excellence over the last three decades.
 Including this one: Before Saturday’s setback to LSU, it was more common for Mark Few’s teams to keep an undefeated record through the third week of February than it was for the Zags to take a loss within the first two weeks of November.
 Both scenarios have now happened twice under the 28th-year coach, who guided the 2016-17 team to a 29-0 record before a Feb. 25 loss to BYU and steered the 2020-21 Zags to 31-0 before coming up short against Baylor in the national championship.
 Meanwhile, only a few members of GU’s current roster were alive the last time the Zags dropped a game on or before Nov. 14. Gonzaga opened Few’s fifth season with a 73-66 loss to Saint Joseph’s – a game that coincidentally also fell on Nov. 14.
 The 2026-27 team might be able to take a thing or two from the way the 2003-04 group responded. The Zags won 28 of their next 29 games, went unbeaten in West Coast Conference play and clinched a No. 2 seed in the NCAA Tournament before losing to Nevada in the second round.
 If the current group wants to chart a similar path, it will start Tuesday at McCarthey Athletic Center against a tough, battle-tested Montana State team that was picked to win the Big Sky Conference last month. The Zags (2-1) and Bobcats (2-2) will tip off at 8 p.m., with former Gonzaga standout Dan Dickau and broadcast partner Rich Walz calling the game for CBS Sports Network.
 Three days after going down to the wire against LSU, Gonzaga may not get much of a respite hosting a Montana State team that ranks No. 114 at KenPom, returns six of its top eight scorers from a team that finished second in the Big Sky standings and has already experienced a hostile road crowd playing BYU at the Marriott Center last Thursday.
 As the transfer portal and name, image and likeness compensation continue to fracture midmajor rosters across the country, former Whitworth coach Matt Logie and Montana State survived the offseason with little disruption. The Bobcats graduated two starters but didn’t lose a single rotation player to the portal and rank No. 14 nationally at KenPom in minutes continuity.
 “It’s certainly something that’s pretty unique in today’s college landscape,” Logie said Monday in a phone interview. “I think what we’ve found at Montana State is there’s still young men out there and families out there that want to be a part of something bigger than themselves and have some self-awareness about where they’re at in their process of development and what they need to do to reach their potential.”
 The Bobcats currently have two players averaging better than 13.0 points per game and two others just shy of the double-digit scoring threshold. Guard Jeremiah Davis and forward Christian King are not only averaging the same scoring total (13.8 ppg), but both also average 4.5 rebounds and 1.8 assists. Point guard Jed Miller, the only returning All-Big Sky First Team player on Montana State’s roster, averages 9.3 ppg to go with 3.0 apg and 2.7 rpg.
 “Those three guys are really what kind of stirs the drink for us in a lot of ways,” Logie said. “But they each kind of do it their own way.”
 A native of Mercer Island, Washington, who spent eight seasons at Whitworth from 2011-19, Logie has diligently recruited the Pacific Northwest during his time at Montana State and has five players from Washington and Oregon.
 “Our pass list is certainly full,” Logie said. “We didn’t have any extra (tickets) to go around. I think we probably could’ve filled up quite a few more seats, but we understand how hard it is to get Zag tickets.”
 A hungry Gonzaga team should be waiting for the Bobcats at the Kennel. Tuesday’s game will be Gonzaga’s final test before a trip to the Players Era 16 next week, and therefore the final chance to rinse the taste of Saturday’s loss.
 Montana State ranks No. 30 nationally in made 3-pointers and could test Gonzaga from the perimeter, but it’s possible the Bobcats will lack the interior size to match a stable of talented Bulldog posts that includes 6-10 Braden Huff (16.5 ppg), 6-10 Izan Almansa (9.5 ppg) and 7-1 Massamba Diop (8.7 ppg).
 “Just with the history of following the program and understanding the way Gonzaga plays, I think you really start with Davis Fogle and Braden Huff as really the Zag constituents that kind of carry the flag both for their culture and what it means to be a Zag,” Logie said. “… As we’ve always seen with Gonzaga teams, they play at one of the best paces in the country. Your transition defense has to be outstanding. They obviously always have tremendous size. … They have that continued ability to hit the paint and the glass.”
